instrument: ECCN 3A090.a
scope: Advanced computing integrated circuits — datacentre AI accelerators and GPUs
parameter: Total processing performance (TPP)
unit: TPP, defined as 2 × MacTOPS × bit length of the operation, aggregated over all processing units on the integrated circuit
alternative: or TPP >= 1600 together with performance density >= 5.92, where performance density is TPP divided by the die area in square millimetres of the logic dies
destinations: Licence required for Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5 that are not also specified in A:5 or A:6 — 44 countries plus Macau. China and Macau are the operative targets.
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau. Since 15 January 2026 applications for parts below TPP 21,000 and total DRAM bandwidth 6,500 GB/s (H200 and MI325X class) are reviewed case by case.
note: This is the master line for AI chips. It catches every current training-class accelerator — H100, H200, B200, MI300 and their successors — because TPP scales with both throughput and the precision at which the part is quoted. It misses nothing at the top and quite a lot in the middle: a chip can be cut below 4800 by trimming clocks or disabling units while keeping most of its usefulness for inference, which is how the H800 and later the H20 were built.

instrument: ECCN 3A090.a alternative parameter
scope: Advanced computing integrated circuits, small-die and chiplet designs
parameter: Performance density (TPP per square millimetre of logic die area)
unit: TPP per mm² of applicable die area
alternative: applies only in combination with TPP >= 1600; caches count towards die area, separate memory stacks such as HBM do not
destinations: Same as 3A090.a — Country Groups D:1, D:4, D:5 not also in A:5 or A:6
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau
note: Added on 17 November 2023 to stop the obvious workaround to a pure throughput cap: build a smaller, cheaper die and ship more of them. It catches efficient small accelerators that a raw TPP line would let through. It is also the parameter most sensitive to packaging choices, because what counts as die area for a chiplet part is a judgement call.

instrument: ECCN 3A090 as first written (7 October 2022 rule)
scope: Advanced computing integrated circuits
parameter: Aggregate bidirectional interconnect transfer rate, combined with bit length × TOPS
unit: GByte/s aggregate bidirectional transfer rate, required together with a bit-length × TOPS product of 4800 or more
alternative: Both conditions had to be met; failing either took a chip out of the entry
destinations: China and Macau
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial
note: Kept in the map because it is the clearest case of a threshold being designed around. Nvidia cut NVLink bandwidth below 600 GB/s to create the A800 and H800, which were legal for a year. BIS deleted the interconnect parameter on 17 November 2023 and the workaround closed.

instrument: ECCN 3A090.b
scope: Mid-range advanced computing integrated circuits — the notified band below 3A090.a
parameter: Total processing performance with performance density
unit: TPP of 2400 or more and less than 4800, together with performance density of 1.6 or more and less than 5.92
alternative: or TPP >= 1600 with performance density >= 3.2 and < 5.92
destinations: Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5 not also in A:5 or A:6
licensePolicy: Eligible for License Exception NAC (Notified Advanced Computing): no licence for D:1 and D:4 destinations; for Macau and D:5 an application must be filed at least 25 calendar days before shipment. Not eligible for the January 2026 case-by-case band, which sits above 3A090.a.
note: The grey band. It exists so that BIS learns about chips just under the main line rather than banning them, and it is what turns the control from a wall into a notification regime for workstation and mid-range parts. It catches gaming and professional cards with real AI throughput; it misses anything a designer can push below TPP 1600.

instrument: ECCN 3A090.c
scope: High bandwidth memory stacks and packages
parameter: Memory bandwidth density
unit: GB per second per square millimetre of package or stack area
alternative: Calculated as the memory bandwidth of the package or stack in GB/s divided by its area in mm²
destinations: Worldwide licence requirement with country-group carve-outs; enforced against China and Macau through the advanced computing foreign direct product rule, which reaches foreign-made HBM
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau
note: Set deliberately low: 2 GB/s/mm² catches every HBM stack in production, including HBM2E, so the entry is a ban on selling HBM into China rather than a performance line. It is the control that bites hardest on Chinese accelerators, because a Chinese AI chip without HBM cannot feed its own compute.

instrument: License Exception HBM, 15 CFR 740.25
scope: HBM shipped to a co-packaging site for incorporation into a designer's product
parameter: Memory bandwidth density ceiling for exception eligibility
unit: GB per second per square millimetre
alternative: Exporter must be headquartered in the US or a Country Group A:5 destination and not have a parent in Macau or D:5; direct purchase by the co-packaged commodity designer and direct shipment to the packaging site, with tracking and confirmation
destinations: Not available for Macau or Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Self-executing exception, no licence application, subject to the conditions above
note: The valve that keeps the legitimate HBM trade flowing while 3A090.c stays broad. The gap between the 2 GB/s/mm² control line and the 3.3 GB/s/mm² exception ceiling is the space in which ordinary HBM3 packaging logistics happen; anything above 3.3 needs a licence even for allied supply chains.

instrument: ECCN 4A090
scope: Computers, electronic assemblies and components containing controlled advanced computing ICs — servers, HGX and OAM baseboards, whole racks
parameter: Contains an integrated circuit meeting or exceeding the 3A090 thresholds
unit: same TPP thresholds as 3A090.a (4800, or 1600 with performance density 5.92); 4A090.b mirrors 3A090.b
alternative: 4A090.a tracks 3A090.a; 4A090.b tracks 3A090.b and inherits its NAC treatment
destinations: Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5 not also in A:5 or A:6
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau; follows the 3A090 policy of the chip inside
note: The system-level mirror of 3A090, and the entry most of the smuggling cases actually turn on, because chips move in servers. It catches assembled AI servers wherever they are built; it misses nothing technically, which is why enforcement against 4A090 is a transshipment problem rather than a classification problem.

instrument: Licence review policy for advanced computing commodities, 15 January 2026 final rule
scope: 3A090.a and 4A090.a items destined for end users in China and Macau
parameter: TPP ceiling for case-by-case review
unit: TPP
alternative: must be met together with total DRAM bandwidth below 6,500 GB/s; named examples are the Nvidia H200 and the AMD MI325X
destinations: China and Macau, for end users located there; presumption of denial retained for entities headquartered in restricted countries and for reexports and transfers
licensePolicy: Moves from presumption of denial to case-by-case review, conditional on certifications that US domestic supply is sufficient, that no domestic orders were delayed, that global foundry capacity is not diverted, that recipients have adequate security procedures, and that independent US-based third-party testing confirms the performance specification
note: The first threshold in the regime that opens a door rather than closing one: it draws a second line above 3A090.a and says everything between them may be sold to China if the conditions hold. It catches the H200 and MI325X; it deliberately excludes Blackwell-class parts, which sit far above TPP 21,000.

instrument: Licence review policy for advanced computing commodities, 15 January 2026 final rule
scope: 3A090.a and 4A090.a items destined for China and Macau
parameter: Total DRAM bandwidth ceiling for case-by-case review
unit: GB/s
alternative: must be met together with TPP below 21,000
destinations: China and Macau
licensePolicy: Case-by-case review when both this and the TPP ceiling are met
note: A memory-bandwidth ceiling used as a proxy for training usefulness, and the first time BIS has drawn a licensing line on DRAM bandwidth rather than on compute. It concedes that a chip's value for large-model work is set as much by how fast it can feed itself as by how fast it can multiply.

instrument: Licence review policy for advanced computing commodities, 15 January 2026 final rule
scope: Volume condition attached to case-by-case licences for China and Macau
parameter: China and Macau shipments as a share of US end-use shipments of the same product
unit: % of the total of that product shipped to customers for end use in the United States
alternative: Applicant must also show that no domestic order was delayed or deprioritised to fill a China-bound order
destinations: China and Macau
licensePolicy: Condition of licence approval; breach of the certification is a licence violation
note: An industrial-policy condition dressed as an export control: China may not receive more than half of what the American market receives of the same part. It ties the size of the permitted China business to the size of the US business, so the cap grows as US data-centre demand grows.

instrument: 15 CFR 744.23(a)(1)(iii) and Part 743 due-diligence rule of 16 January 2025
scope: Advanced logic dies at foundries and OSATs — the presumption that an unidentified advanced die is a 3A090 chip
parameter: Approximated transistor count (transistor density × die area in mm²)
unit: transistors on a logic die made at the 16/14 nm node or below, or with a non-planar transistor architecture
alternative: Rises to 35 billion for shipments in 2027 and 40 billion from 2029; the earlier red-flag figure was 50 billion
destinations: Worldwide licence presumption for front-end fabricators and OSATs, rebuttable by shipping to an approved IC designer, an approved OSAT, or on a designer attestation
licensePolicy: Presumption that a licence is required unless overcome; Approved IC Designer status runs for 180 days from submission, with applications required after 13 April 2026
note: The rule that pushed the control back one stage, from the chip designer to the foundry that prints the wafer. Instead of asking what a die does, it asks how many transistors it has, which a foundry always knows. It is the answer to shell-company design houses ordering Nvidia-class dies at TSMC; it misses dies below the transistor line and anything made on mature nodes.

instrument: Definition of "advanced-node integrated circuits", 15 CFR 772.1, applied through 15 CFR 744.23
scope: Logic fabs — the end-use trigger for equipment, parts and services
parameter: Production technology node, or transistor architecture
unit: nanometres (16/14 nm node or less), or any non-planar transistor architecture (FinFET, gate-all-around) at any node
alternative: The architecture prong has no number: a planar 20 nm line is outside, a non-planar 22 nm line is inside
destinations: Facilities located in Macau or a Country Group D:5 destination
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for facilities in China and Macau that produce advanced-node ICs; case-by-case for others
note: The line that decides whether a Chinese fab can buy tools at all. It catches SMIC's N+2 and N+3 lines and every FinFET line in China; it misses the enormous mature-node build-out at 28 nm and above, which is why Chinese capacity has grown fastest just below this number.

instrument: Definition of "advanced-node integrated circuits", 15 CFR 772.1
scope: NAND flash fabs
parameter: Number of memory layers
unit: layers of NOT-AND (NAND) memory
alternative: None; a single-number test
destinations: Facilities in Macau or Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau facilities producing at or above the line
note: The only threshold in the regime that is a plain count rather than a derived metric, and the easiest to verify by teardown. It catches YMTC's Xtacking lines; it has not moved since October 2022 even though the industry has gone from 128 to more than 300 layers, so the line now sits well below the state of the art.

instrument: Definition of "advanced-node integrated circuits", 15 CFR 772.1
scope: DRAM fabs, including the DRAM dies that become HBM
parameter: Memory cell area, memory density, or through-silicon vias per die
unit: µm² memory cell area; or memory density greater than 0.20 gigabits per mm²; or more than 3,000 through-silicon vias per die
alternative: Originally written as a half-pitch of 18 nanometres or less; replaced on 2 December 2024 by these three physical measures, which BIS said match real 18 nm-class production rather than the theoretical IRDS model. The earlier numbers were a cell area below 0.0019 µm² and a density above 0.288 Gb/mm².
destinations: Facilities in Macau or Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau facilities producing at or above the line
note: The clearest example of a threshold being rewritten because it did not survive contact with a fab. Half-pitch is a marketing number; cell area, bit density and TSV count are measurable on a die. The TSV prong was added specifically so that HBM base dies cannot escape by being coarse in-plane.

instrument: Definition of "supercomputer", 15 CFR 772.1, applied through 15 CFR 744.23
scope: Whole computing systems, and any item destined to develop, produce, operate or maintain one
parameter: Collective maximum theoretical compute capacity within a bounded physical envelope
unit: double-precision (64-bit) petaflops, or 200 or more single-precision (32-bit) petaflops, within an envelope of 41,600 cubic feet or smaller
alternative: Either the double-precision or the single-precision figure triggers the definition
destinations: Macau and Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Licence required for any item subject to the EAR with knowledge of a supercomputer end use in Macau or D:5; presumption of denial
note: A catch-all that works on installations rather than parts: even uncontrolled components need a licence if you know they are going into a Chinese machine of this size. The volume test, 41,600 cubic feet, is roughly a large machine room, and it is what stops the rule from being evaded by spreading the same compute across a bigger building.

scope: DUV lithography scanners — the immersion tools that print advanced logic without EUV
parameter: Maximum dedicated chuck overlay, for tools with a light source wavelength of 193 nm or longer
unit: nanometres dedicated chuck overlay (3B001.f.1.b.1); a second tier covers overlay greater than 1.50 nm but 2.4 nm or less (3B001.f.1.b.2)
alternative: EUV tools — light source below 193 nm — are controlled separately and more tightly
destinations: Macau and Country Group D:5, the scope to which the October 2023 rule extended semiconductor manufacturing equipment controls from the earlier China-only formulation
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau
note: Overlay, not resolution, is the parameter that separates a usable advanced-logic scanner from a mature-node one, because multipatterning lives or dies on layer-to-layer alignment. The 1.50 nm tier tracks ASML's top immersion tools and the 2.4 nm tier reaches down into the older immersion fleet the Dutch controls also cover.

instrument: 15 CFR 734.4 de minimis rule as applied to ECCN 3B001.f.1.b.2.b
scope: Foreign-made lithography equipment containing US content
parameter: De minimis US-origin content threshold
unit: % US-origin controlled content
alternative: Standard de minimis for D:5 is 25% for most items and 10% for some; here any US content at all makes the foreign tool subject to the EAR, unless the exporting country controls the item itself — currently only Japan
destinations: For the development or production of advanced-node integrated circuits, in Macau or Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial
note: A zero threshold is the strongest form an export control takes: it converts every American screw, laser or controller inside a foreign scanner into US jurisdiction. It is aimed squarely at ASML and at any future non-US scanner builder, and its carve-out for countries with equivalent controls is the mechanism that rewards allied alignment.

instrument: ECCN 3B001.c.1.a and 3B001.c.1.c
scope: Plasma dry etch tools — the high-aspect-ratio etch needed for 3D NAND, DRAM capacitors and gate-all-around structures
parameter: Equipment designed or modified for isotropic dry etching (c.1.a) or anisotropic dry etching (c.1.c)
unit: process capability, not a numeric parameter — control is by function and by the advanced-node end use it enables
alternative: Atomic layer etching tools were added to the CCL by the 6 September 2024 rule and further paragraphs (k through n, p) were brought under national security controls on 2 December 2024
destinations: Worldwide national security and regional stability controls; licence required for Macau and Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau
note: Unlike the chip entries, most etch controls are functional rather than numeric: BIS names the process, not a performance figure, because etch capability is hard to reduce to one number. That makes the entry broad and hard to design around, and it is the reason Chinese etch suppliers such as AMEC became a national priority.

instrument: ECCN 3B001.d (formerly ECCN 3B090)
scope: Deposition tools — CVD, ALD, electroless and electroplating equipment for advanced interconnect and 3D structures
parameter: Deposition process capability, by sub-paragraph
unit: process capability; 3B090's tool list was folded into 3B001.d.1, d.2 and d.12 on 17 November 2023
alternative: Physical vapour deposition controls that had been in 3B090.a.6 were dropped in the same rule; area-selective deposition and atomic layer deposition were added by the 6 September 2024 rule
destinations: Macau and Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau
note: The clearest sign that the control map is drawn around processes, not products: ECCN 3B090 was invented in October 2022 as a China-only entry and then dissolved into the general 3B001 list a year later, which multilateralised it. It catches tungsten and cobalt fill and ALD; it does not catch the older deposition tools that make up most of a mature-node fab.

instrument: ECCN 3B001.q
scope: EUV masks and reticles for integrated circuits
parameter: Designed for EUV lithography
unit: no numeric parameter — control is by EUV designation
alternative: EUV pellicles were separately controlled by Japan in July 2023
destinations: Worldwide national security and regional stability controls; licence for Macau and Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau
note: A control on the consumable rather than the machine. Since no EUV scanner has ever been exported to China, controlling EUV masks looks redundant, but it forecloses a route in which China builds or acquires a scanner and then needs a mask supply chain it does not have.

instrument: ECCN 3B002.c
scope: Inspection equipment designed for EUV mask blanks or EUV patterned masks
parameter: Designed for EUV mask blank or patterned mask inspection
unit: no numeric parameter
alternative: 3B002 otherwise covers stored-program-controlled test equipment for finished or unfinished semiconductor devices
destinations: National security and regional stability controls; licence for Macau and Country Group D:5. 3B002.c is also within the product scope of the semiconductor manufacturing equipment foreign direct product rule.
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial for China and Macau
note: One of only two ECCNs — with 3B001.a.4 — that the December 2024 semiconductor equipment foreign direct product rule names in its product scope, which makes actinic mask inspection one of the two narrowest and hardest points in the whole equipment fence.

instrument: Advanced computing foreign direct product rule, 15 CFR 734.9(h)
scope: Foreign-made chips and computers that never touched the United States
parameter: Product scope test — the item is a direct product of controlled US technology or software, or was made by a plant that is itself such a direct product
unit: classification test: foreign-produced items classified in ECCNs 3A090, 4A090 and the associated .z paragraphs
alternative: Destination scope is met by knowledge that the item is destined for Macau or Country Group D:5, or is designed by an entity headquartered there, or is for the production of a mask, wafer or die for such an entity
destinations: Macau and Country Group D:5, plus entity-headquartered tests that reach worldwide
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial
note: This is what makes the American control map extraterritorial. A chip designed in China and fabricated in Taiwan on tools built in Japan is still subject to US law, because somewhere in the toolchain sits US technology. It has no numeric threshold of its own; it borrows 3A090's.

instrument: Semiconductor manufacturing equipment foreign direct product rule, 15 CFR 734.9(k)
scope: Foreign-made chipmaking equipment
parameter: Product scope test, tied to two ECCNs
unit: foreign-produced items classified in ECCN 3B001.a.4 or ECCN 3B002.c
alternative: Destination scope is Macau or Country Group D:5. A companion de minimis change makes any US-origin integrated circuit inside a foreign tool enough to bring it under the EAR.
destinations: Macau and Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial
note: Deliberately narrow: two ECCNs, not the whole 3B001 list, because a broad equipment FDPR would have hit allied toolmakers hardest. It reaches equipment that has never been near the United States and is the legal basis on which BIS can stop a Japanese or Dutch tool at the Chinese border.

instrument: Footnote 5 entity list foreign direct product rule, 15 CFR 734.9(e)(3)
scope: Foreign-made semiconductor equipment and related items going to designated Chinese fabs and toolmakers
parameter: Entity designation plus product scope in Category 3B
unit: classification test against Footnote 5 designations on the Entity List
alternative: Parallel to Footnote 1, which was created for Huawei in 2020 and reaches any foreign chip made with US equipment
destinations: Entities designated with Footnote 5 on the Entity List, wherever located
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial
note: A named-entity version of the equipment rule: instead of drawing a technical line, it draws a list. The December 2024 package attached it to a batch of 140 Entity List additions, which is how the equipment fence became a fence around specific Chinese companies rather than a specification.

instrument: Affiliates rule, 15 CFR 744 (interim final rule of 29 September 2025)
scope: Subsidiaries and affiliates of listed entities that are not themselves listed
parameter: Ownership by one or more listed entities
unit: % ownership, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate
alternative: Applies to the Entity List, the Military End User list, and specified OFAC SDN designations under 15 CFR 744.8. Where several listed owners have different licence requirements, the most restrictive applies. No de minimis below 50%.
destinations: Worldwide — the test is ownership, not location
licensePolicy: The affiliate inherits the licence requirements and review policy of its most restricted listed owner
note: The single largest expansion of the Entity List's reach, and the fastest reversal: stayed on 10 November 2025 as part of the one-year US-China truce and due to snap back on 9 November 2026 unless extended. Watch this date — it is the most consequential scheduled event in the map.

instrument: One-year suspension of the affiliates rule
scope: The 50% ownership test above
parameter: Duration of the stay
unit: months — amendments to 15 CFR parts 732, 734, 736, 744 and 748 stayed until 9 November 2026
alternative: Automatic reimposition on expiry unless BIS extends it
destinations: Worldwide
licensePolicy: During the stay, unlisted affiliates are treated as they were before 29 September 2025
note: Listed as its own entry because the expiry date is itself a governing number. It was traded against China's suspension of the October 2025 rare-earth licensing regime, which means the two suspensions are linked and are likely to end together.

instrument: Ministerial order under the Strategic Goods Decree, in force 1 September 2023
scope: Advanced immersion DUV lithography systems
parameter: ASML TWINSCAN model line
unit: TWINSCAN NXT:2000i and subsequent immersion systems
alternative: EUV systems were already under licence before this order
destinations: Worldwide national licence requirement administered by the Dutch government, aimed at China
licensePolicy: Case-by-case; in practice licences for Chinese advanced-logic destinations have not been granted
note: The Dutch line is drawn by model number rather than by a physical parameter, which makes it unusually easy to police and unusually easy to see. NXT:2000i is where ASML's overlay performance crosses into the range that supports multipatterned advanced logic.

instrument: Ministerial order amendment, Staatscourant 2024, 29008, in force 7 September 2024
scope: Older immersion DUV lithography systems
parameter: ASML TWINSCAN model line, extended downwards
unit: TWINSCAN NXT:1970i and NXT:1980i added to the licensed list
alternative: The same order transferred licensing authority for these models from the United States to the Netherlands
destinations: Worldwide national licence requirement, aimed at China
licensePolicy: Case-by-case, decided in The Hague rather than Washington
note: The government.nl announcement describes the measure but does not name the models; the NXT:1970i and NXT:1980i identifications come from TrendForce and CNBC. The significance is jurisdictional as much as technical: the Netherlands took the licensing decision back from the United States for tools it builds.

instrument: Amendment to the Export Trade Control Order under FEFTA, announced 23 May 2023, in force 23 July 2023
scope: Advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment, test equipment, masks and reticles, and EUV pellicles
parameter: Number of newly controlled equipment categories
unit: categories of equipment, controlled by specified technology or by performance above a stated threshold
alternative: Categories span cleaning, deposition, annealing, lithography, etch and inspection/test
destinations: All countries and regions. A simplified bulk licence is available for 42 friendly destinations including the United States, South Korea and Taiwan; individual licences are required elsewhere, which in practice means China.
licensePolicy: Individual licence, case-by-case, for non-Group-A destinations
note: Japan's contribution to the fence, and the reason the US zero de minimis rule for lithography has a carve-out for Japanese-controlled items. Written as a country-neutral list to avoid naming China, which is why it applies worldwide and then exempts the 42 destinations Japan trusts.

instrument: Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion, ECCN 3A090/4A090 country allocations
scope: Cumulative installed base of advanced computing ICs in a Tier 2 country
parameter: Country-level TPP allocation through 2027
unit: TPP, cumulative maximum per country
alternative: Presumption of approval up to the allocation; presumption of denial above it and for Macau and Country Group D:5
destinations: All destinations outside the 18 Tier 1 allies and outside D:5
licensePolicy: Rescinded before it was enforced
note: The most ambitious threshold ever written into the regime: a numeric compute quota for entire countries. Published 15 January 2025, never enforced, rescinded 13 May 2025 with BIS instructing enforcement officials to stand down before the 15 May compliance date. Kept here because the numbers define what a compute quota would look like if one returns.

instrument: Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion, National Validated End User allocations
scope: Per-company, per-country cumulative compute for validated data-centre operators
parameter: Cumulative TPP allocation, ramped by quarter
unit: TPP by 2027, rising from 633,000,000 in Q1 2025 through 1,899,000,000 in Q1 2026
alternative: Eligibility limited to entities in Country Groups A, B and D:1 to D:4, excluding Macau and D:5
destinations: Outside the Tier 1 allies and outside D:5
licensePolicy: Rescinded before it was enforced
note: The schedule is the interesting part: allocations rose eightfold over three years, an explicit assumption about how fast the world outside the allied core should be allowed to grow its compute. No later rule has replaced that assumption with another number.

instrument: Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion, Universal Validated End User conditions
scope: Global cloud and AI companies headquartered in Tier 1 countries
parameter: Share of a company's total AI computing power permitted outside Tier 1 destinations
unit: % of total AI computing power outside the Tier 1 list, with no more than 7% in any single country outside it
alternative: US-headquartered UVEUs could not place more than 50% of their total AI computing power outside the United States
destinations: Anywhere except Macau and Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Rescinded before it was enforced
note: A control on where American compute physically sits rather than on who buys it. The 50% domestic-retention condition for US firms reappears in a different form in the January 2026 H200 rule, which suggests the idea survived the rescission even though the rule did not.

instrument: License Exception LPP (Low Processing Performance) under the AI Diffusion framework
scope: Small orders of advanced computing ICs to ordinary commercial buyers
parameter: Annual TPP per ultimate consignee
unit: TPP of advanced computing ICs per calendar year to any individual ultimate consignee
alternative: Direct exports only, no distributors; not available for Macau or D:5
destinations: Outside Macau and Country Group D:5
licensePolicy: Rescinded before it was enforced
note: Roughly the compute of a few thousand top-end accelerators a year: the line the rule drew between a research group and a national programme. It is the only place the regime has ever tried to say how much AI compute an ordinary customer should be able to buy without a licence.

instrument: Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion, control on closed model weights
scope: Trained weights of closed-weight AI models — the first US export control on a model rather than a chip
parameter: Cumulative training compute
unit: computational operations used to train the model
alternative: Open-weight models were excluded
destinations: Worldwide licence requirement
licensePolicy: Presumption of denial; rescinded before it was enforced
note: The seam between chip governance and model governance, and the only time the two have been written into the same instrument. It borrowed the 10^26 figure from the 2023 executive order's reporting threshold, which shows how quickly a reporting number becomes a control number.

instrument: Enhanced favourable treatment for the United Arab Emirates, final rule of 10 July 2026
scope: Country-group treatment of the UAE for advanced computing and other dual-use items
parameter: Country group reclassification
unit: moved into Country Group A:5; removed from Country Groups D:3 and D:4
alternative: Licence requirements for ECCN 3A090.a and 4A090.a are retained for the UAE except where the ultimate consignee and end user is a UAE government entity or an approved commercial entity listed in Supplement No. 8 to Part 740 — currently two UAE firms (G42 and Core42) and eight US-headquartered AI companies with their subsidiaries. Strategic Trade Authorization becomes available for approved entities.
destinations: United Arab Emirates
licensePolicy: Case-by-case with written assurances; authorisation for the two UAE-headquartered firms expires on 6 April 2027 unless they become US-headquartered
note: The mechanism that replaced the AI Diffusion tiers: instead of a compute quota per country, a named list of approved companies per country. It catches the diversion risk by identity rather than by volume, and the April 2027 expiry for G42 and Core42 makes American incorporation the price of continued access.

instrument: Presidential proclamation adjusting imports of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and derivative products
scope: Imports of advanced computing chips and listed derivative products into the United States
parameter: Ad valorem duty rate
unit: % ad valorem on covered products described in the Annex
alternative: Exempt uses include US data centres, repairs and replacements performed in the US, US research and development, startups, non-data-centre consumer and civil industrial applications, and US public-sector applications
destinations: All imports into the United States
licensePolicy: Not a licence: a duty. The Secretary was directed to report by 1 July 2026 on whether the data-centre treatment should change.
note: The point at which the regime stopped being purely about denial and started being about price. It shares an effective date with the H200 licensing band, and the two work together: China may buy the chip, and the chip is taxed on the way in. The data-centre carve-out is what stops the tariff falling on American AI build-out.

instrument: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 51(2)
scope: General-purpose AI models — the model layer that the chip controls ultimately govern
parameter: Cumulative training compute
unit: floating point operations (FLOP) used for training
alternative: A rebuttable presumption of high-impact capability and therefore systemic risk. Providers may notify the Commission with evidence that their model does not pose systemic risk; the Commission may also designate a model below the threshold.
destinations: Providers placing general-purpose AI models on the EU market, wherever they are established
licensePolicy: Not a licence: notification within two weeks under Article 52, plus systemic-risk obligations — model evaluation, adversarial testing, incident reporting and cybersecurity protection
note: The only compute threshold in the map that is in force on the model side, and it sits an order of magnitude below the US figure. Commission enforcement powers over GPAI providers began on 2 August 2026, and Article 51(3) lets the Commission move the number by delegated act — which makes it the most likely of all these figures to change without a legislature.

instrument: Proposed rule, Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters (89 FR 73612)
scope: Developers of dual-use foundation models
parameter: Cumulative training compute
unit: computational operations, integer or floating point, counting one multiply-accumulate as two operations
alternative: A lower threshold of 10^23 operations was proposed for models trained primarily on biological sequence data
destinations: US persons and companies; a reporting duty, not an export control
licensePolicy: Quarterly reporting to BIS. Proposed 11 September 2024 with the comment period closing 11 October 2024; never finalised. Its authority, Executive Order 14110, was revoked by Executive Order 14179 on 23 January 2025.
note: As of September 2026 the United States has no compute-based reporting threshold in force for AI models, only for the chips that train them. This is the gap in the map: the chip side is governed to five significant figures and the model side is not governed at all.

instrument: Proposed rule, Establishment of Reporting Requirements (89 FR 73612), computing cluster prong
scope: Owners and operators of large-scale computing clusters
parameter: Networking transit rate together with theoretical maximum compute
unit: computational operations per second for AI training without sparsity, in machines transitively connected by data centre networking greater than 300 Gbit/s
alternative: Both the networking and the compute condition must be met
destinations: US persons and companies
licensePolicy: Quarterly reporting; never finalised
note: The only US threshold ever drawn on a data centre rather than a chip or a model, and the only one that uses interconnect bandwidth as a governing parameter — the same idea BIS abandoned in ECCN 3A090 in November 2023 because it was too easy to design around.

instrument: MOFCOM Announcement 2025 No. 61, extraterritorial controls on medium and heavy rare earths
scope: Foreign-made goods containing Chinese-origin controlled rare earth material, including magnets and materials used in chipmaking equipment
parameter: Chinese-origin controlled content by value
unit: % of the value of the foreign-made item
alternative: A mirror of the US de minimis and foreign direct product logic, applied to materials rather than technology
destinations: Worldwide, with a licence requirement enforced against re-export to designated end uses including advanced semiconductors
licensePolicy: Licence required; suspended for one year from 10 November 2025 under the US-China truce, alongside the US suspension of the affiliates rule
note: Included because it is the only non-US threshold in the map that reaches outside its own jurisdiction, and because 0.1% is stricter than any American de minimis figure except the zero applied to lithography. Its suspension expires at the same time as the affiliates rule stay, which is why the two must be read together.
